6377.stem:
Two teams of athletes were compared on their endurance, as measured by the number of repetitions that they could complete of a short, mixed-activity training circuit. The results are shown in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf-plot below.

\exfigure{308_q17_1}

figures.cap: back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot, Team A and Team B

parts.latex: What was the difference between the two teams in terms of the median number of repetitions?
Given that Team B has an interquartile range of 16, show that Team A has a larger interquartile range, and explain what this means in terms of statistical comparison.

solutions.latex:
Reading the plot, Team A has 13 scores:
$$5, 6, 8, 14, 17, 17, 18, 20, 22, 27, 31, 33, 40$$
The median is the 7th score, $18$.

Team B has 12 scores:
$$2, 6, 13, 17, 19, 22, 24, 25, 28, 34, 36, 37$$
The median is the mean of the 6th and 7th scores:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{22 + 24}{2} &= 23 \end{aligned}$$
Difference in medians:
$$\begin{aligned} 23 - 18 &= 5 \end{aligned}$$
The medians differ by $5$ repetitions (Team B higher).

meta.self_check: Re-read stem-and-leaf: A n=13 median 18; B n=12 median 23.

solutions.latex:
For Team A (13 scores), the median is the 7th score. The lower half is the first six scores $5, 6, 8, 14, 17, 17$, so
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 &= \dfrac{8 + 14}{2} \\ &= 11 \end{aligned}$$
The upper half is the last six scores $20, 22, 27, 31, 33, 40$, so
$$\begin{aligned} Q_3 &= \dfrac{27 + 31}{2} \\ &= 29 \end{aligned}$$
Interquartile range of Team A:
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= 29 - 11 \\ &= 18 \end{aligned}$$
Since $18 > 16$, Team A has the larger interquartile range.

This means the middle $50\%$ of Team A's results are more spread out, so Team A is less consistent than Team B.
criteria: Finds $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ for Team A, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Team B IQR computed independently as 31-15=16, matching the given value.

308_q17_1.notes: Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot drawn in TikZ as a plot, not a grid table (12 Nov ruling). It has the Team A and Team B headings, one rule under the headings, and two vertical rules either side of the stem column. The leaf columns and rows are at the crop's positions with identical values. Lines are 0.6pt where the scan's look heavier (rule 3). Rules: 3, 6b.

6778.stem:
The monthly maximum temperature for Sydney and Melbourne are drawn in the boxplots below.

\exfigure{828_q19_1}

parts.latex: What is the median maximum temperature for Sydney?
Calculate the interquartile range for Melbourne.
Which city has more consistent maximum temperatures? Justify your answer by comparing one measure of spread.

solutions.latex:
From the Sydney box plot, the median is
$$24^\circ\text{C}$$

The interquartile range is $Q_3 - Q_1$ for Melbourne.
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= 25 - 16 \\ &= 9^\circ\text{C} \end{aligned}$$

Comparing the interquartile ranges:
$$\text{Sydney } IQR = 5^\circ\text{C} < \text{Melbourne } IQR = 9^\circ\text{C}$$
Or, comparing the ranges:
$$\text{Sydney range} = 9^\circ\text{C} < \text{Melbourne range} = 13^\circ\text{C}$$
Therefore Sydney has more consistent temperatures.

828_q19_1.notes: Two box plots at 0.9pt with grey fill (rule 9): Sydney 17/20/24/25/26 and Melbourne 14/16/21/25/27, on a 12 to 30 scale with light vertical gridlines. Left out the scan's very faint horizontal lines. Title at \footnotesize to match the crop. Overlay 0.88/0.874.

7440.stem:
The back-to-back stem and leaf plots below compare the points Perry scored in playing two games called Zeros and Cyphers 20 times each.

\exfigure{264_q28_1}

figures.cap: back-to-back stem and leaf plot, Zeros (left) and Cyphers (right)

parts.latex: On which game was his median greater and by how much?
Compare the lower quartiles for each game and give the difference.
Which game had the greater interquartile range, and what was the difference?

solutions.latex:
Reading the plot with Zeros on the left and Cyphers on the right, each has 20 scores. The median is the mean of the 10th and 11th scores.

Zeros in order: $5, 7, 8, 14, 16, 16, 17, 19, 20, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28, 31, 33, 35, 45, 47, 52$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Median} &= \dfrac{22+24}{2} = 23 \end{aligned}$$
Cyphers in order: $8, 13, 17, 21, 24, 28, 32, 34, 38, 38, 38, 39, 42, 44, 47, 49, 49, 52, 54, 56$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Median} &= \dfrac{38+38}{2} = 38 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{The median was greater for Cyphers, by } 38 - 23 = 15 \text{ points.}$$

meta.self_check: Counted 20 values each side from the figure; medians 23 and 38.
meta.generated_note: Assumes Zeros is the left side of the plot and Cyphers the right (order of names in the question).

solutions.latex:
The lower quartile is the median of the lowest 10 scores, the mean of the 5th and 6th scores.

Zeros: lowest 10 are $5, 7, 8, 14, 16, 16, 17, 19, 20, 22$
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 &= \dfrac{16+16}{2} = 16 \end{aligned}$$
Cyphers: lowest 10 are $8, 13, 17, 21, 24, 28, 32, 34, 38, 38$
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 &= \dfrac{24+28}{2} = 26 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{The lower quartile of Cyphers (26) is greater than that of Zeros (16), by } 10 \text{ points.}$$

meta.generated_note: Assumes Zeros is the left side.

solutions.latex:
The upper quartile is the median of the highest 10 scores, the mean of the 15th and 16th scores overall (5th and 6th of the top 10).

Zeros: top 10 are $24, 25, 27, 28, 31, 33, 35, 45, 47, 52$
$$\begin{aligned} Q_3 &= \dfrac{31+33}{2} = 32 \end{aligned}$$
Cyphers: top 10 are $38, 39, 42, 44, 47, 49, 49, 52, 54, 56$
$$\begin{aligned} Q_3 &= \dfrac{47+49}{2} = 48 \end{aligned}$$
Interquartile range $= Q_3 - Q_1$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Zeros: } & 32 - 16 = 16 \\ \text{Cyphers: } & 48 - 26 = 22 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Cyphers had the greater interquartile range, by } 22-16 = 6 \text{ points.}$$
criteria: Finds one interquartile range correctly, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Assumes Zeros is the left side.

264_q28_1.notes: Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot drawn in TikZ, not as a table: the top rule and two vertical rules either side of the stems, as on the paper (12 Nov stem-and-leaf ruling). Leaves are transcribed exactly: 20 values on each side, at the crop's column spacing. Round 2 fixed the row spacing. Rules 1, 2, 6b.

7581.stem:
The dot plot shows the waiting times of 50 people ordering a take-away coffee from a local café.

\exfigure{1264_q29_1}

figures.cap: dot plot of waiting times in minutes

parts.latex:
Copy and complete the following table

\extable{1264_q29_t1}

How many scores are outliers?

Support your answer with mathematical calculations.

solutions.latex:
Reading the five-number summary from the dot plot:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Min} & Q_1 & \text{Median} & Q_3 & \text{Max}\\ \hline 1 & 4 & 5 & 7 & 16\\ \hline\end{array}$$
criteria: Some correct values, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: Source: all correct for 2 marks; $-1$ per error to zero.

solutions.latex:
Outliers lie outside the fences $Q_1-1.5\times IQR$ and $Q_3+1.5\times IQR$.

Upper fence:
$$\begin{aligned} Q_3+1.5\times 3 &= 7+4.5 \\ &= 11.5 \end{aligned}$$
Three scores are above 11.5, so there are 3 outliers above.

Lower fence:
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1-1.5\times 3 &= 4-4.5 \\ &= -0.5 \end{aligned}$$
No score is below $-0.5$, so there are no outliers below.
$$\therefore\ \text{There are 3 outliers}$$
criteria: Finds one fence correctly with its conclusion, or equivalent merit

1264_q29_1.notes: Dot plot of the 50 waiting times. Column counts: 1:3, 2:5, 3:3, 4:10, 5:6, 6:9, 7:5, 8:1, 9:3, 10:1, 11:1, 12:1, 15:1, 16:1, which add up to 50. Dots are grey-filled with a black outline, on a light grid. Axes have no arrows, like the crop. Tick labels and titles are bold as on the paper; titles were made smaller in round 2. The redraw score is low only because of the faint grey grid; the dots, axes and labels line up.
